parsed_response.reasoning: The diff explicitly adds `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in Post#cook, which executes before the existing `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. The mechanism described is verifiable: any plugin hooking after_post_cook (e.g., to sanitize/transform cooked HTML) is silently skipped for exactly those posts — and TopicEmbed.import sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` on content pulled from external RSS feeds, which the diff also shows is rendered with `raw post.cooked` in embed/best.html.erb. Whether this bypass is intentional (the comment says 'we can skip the rendering pipeline') makes it arguable as design, but the described behavior is real and grounded in the diff.

judged_text: The new raw_html branch of Post#cook returns before Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook), so plugins registered on that filter silently never run on imported posts. Plugin authors whose after_post_cook hooks transform or sanitize cooked HTML are silently bypassed by exactly the posts carrying unsanitized external feed HTML — a site relying on such a plugin for HTML policy has raw feed content rendered unfiltered.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now has an early return for raw_html: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the subsequent `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. The diff also shows imported/embed content explicitly sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (TopicEmbed.import via PostCreator), meaning those posts will never run the `:after_post_cook` plugin hooks. This is a real behavior change introduced by the diff and matches the finding’s concern about plugins being silently bypassed specifically for imported external HTML.
